events.description: Learner picked a plate boundary type (convergent, divergent, or transform); resets advance progress.

events.name: LEARN_STEP
events.description: One step of the transport clock or Step button (from the composed std-learn-transport trait); advances plate motion by one step and recomputes landforms, earthquakes, and geometry — the same computation the tick used to run — and caps at maxAdvanceSteps.

events.name: LEARN_RESET
events.description: Transport Reset broadcast (from the composed std-learn-transport trait); reseeds boundary selection, advance progress, and motion geometry from config.

events.name: LEARN_UPDATED
events.description: Transport state broadcast on load and Run/Pause toggle (from the composed std-learn-transport trait); repaints the full shell so the strip's Run/Pause label and step caption stay fresh.

events.name: PLATES_3D_UPDATED
events.description: Fires on INIT/MODE_SELECTED and every tour update with the active boundary preset, the currently selected feature's id, name, and caption, plus visited/total tour progress — a composed listener (readout, quiz) can subscribe; a harmless no-op when the atom runs standalone.
events.synonyms: subduction, tectonic plates, trench, convection, convergent, 3d

events.name: SYNC_STATIONS
events.description: Roster hot-swap relay into the composed Learn3DTour atom — STEP emits the newly selected preset's stations/edges/backdrop here so the tour trait (single writer of the roster and progress fields) adopts them and restarts the tour at the first new station.
events.synonyms: subduction, tectonic plates, trench, convection, convergent, 3d

events.name: MODE_SELECTED
events.description: Lab router broadcast naming the active mode; this instrument renders when the mode equals matchMode, otherwise renders null.

events.name: TOUR_3D_UPDATED
events.description: Tour-state broadcast from the composed Learn3DTour atom — every Tour/click/Reset/roster-swap lands here (bare-event cascade, same delivery as the lab routers) so the preset-aware full shell repaints over the fresh tour selection; the sibling is the one visible render authority, with the tour shell embedded.

events.description: Lab router broadcast naming the active mode; this instrument renders when the mode equals matchMode, otherwise renders null.

events.description: Learner picked a consonant button; the matching place × manner cell lights up and its symbol and example word are shown.

events.name: ANSWER_QUIZ
events.description: Learner answered the quiz prompt by choosing a manner of articulation for the shown symbol; scored when not already answered.

events.name: NEXT_QUIZ
events.description: Learner advanced the quiz to the next symbol, clearing the answered flag and feedback.

events.name: MORPHOLOGY_UPDATED
events.description: The word-builder state after each learner action — a composed listener (readout, grader) can subscribe; a harmless no-op when the atom runs standalone.
events.synonyms: morphology update, morpheme attached, word built, gloss check

events.name: MODE_SELECTED
events.description: Lab router broadcast naming the active mode; this instrument renders when the mode equals matchMode, otherwise renders null.

events.name: ATTACH_MORPHEME
events.description: Learner attached a morpheme from the bank to the right edge of the growing word; the attachment is judged against the order and category constraints.

events.name: REMOVE
events.description: Learner removed the most recently attached morpheme from the word.

events.name: CHECK_WORD
events.description: Learner asked whether the built sequence is an attested word; the concatenated forms are looked up in the gloss table.

events.name: RESET
events.description: Learner cleared the word back to empty, removing every attached morpheme.

events.name: SOUNDCHANGE_UPDATED
events.description: The sound-change state after each learner action — a composed listener (readout, grader) can subscribe; a harmless no-op when the atom runs standalone.
events.synonyms: sound change update, rule applied, vowel shift progress, Great Vowel Shift step

events.name: MODE_SELECTED
events.description: Lab router broadcast naming the active mode; this instrument renders when the mode equals matchMode, otherwise renders null.

events.name: APPLY_CHANGE
events.description: Learner applied the next ordered sound-change rule, striking every word whose current vowel matches it.

events.name: RESET_CHANGES
events.description: Learner reset all words back to their original vowels, undoing every applied rule.

events.name: SYNTAXTREE_UPDATED
events.description: The parse-tree state after each learner action — a composed listener (readout, grader) can subscribe; a harmless no-op when the atom runs standalone.
events.synonyms: syntax tree update, constituent attached, parse progress, derivation step

events.name: MODE_SELECTED
events.description: Lab router broadcast naming the active mode; this instrument renders when the mode equals matchMode, otherwise renders null.

events.name: ATTACH
events.description: Learner pressed a constituent-category button to attach the next bottom-up derivation step to the parse tree.

events.name: RESET_TREE
events.description: Learner reset the current sentence's parse tree back to just the words, clearing all built constituents.

events.name: NEXT_SENTENCE
events.description: Learner advanced to the next sentence in the roster, resetting the parse tree.

events.name: VOWELS_UPDATED
events.description: The vowel-space state after each learner action — a composed listener (readout, grader) can subscribe; a harmless no-op when the atom runs standalone.
events.synonyms: vowel update, formant change, F1 F2, nearest cardinal vowel, vowel quadrilateral

events.name: MODE_SELECTED
events.description: Lab router broadcast naming the active mode; this instrument renders when the mode equals matchMode, otherwise renders null.

events.name: SET_FORMANTS
events.description: Learner stepped F1 (tongue height) or F2 (tongue backness); the vowel point moves and the nearest cardinal vowel is recomputed.

events.name: LOAD_INVENTORY
events.description: Learner switched to another vowel inventory (e.g. from cardinal vowels to the English vowel system).

events.name: TOGGLE_ROUNDING
events.description: Learner flipped lip rounding; the visible vowel set and nearest-vowel computation switch between unrounded and rounded vowels.

events.name: CONDITIONING_UPDATED
events.description: The conditioning state after each learner action — a composed listener (readout, grader) can subscribe; a harmless no-op when the atom runs standalone.
events.synonyms: conditioning update, associative strength, acquisition, extinction, trial result

events.name: MODE_SELECTED
events.description: Lab router broadcast naming the active mode; this instrument renders when the mode equals matchMode, otherwise renders null.

events.name: RUN_PAIRING
events.description: Learner ran a CS+US pairing trial, driving associative strength toward the asymptote via the Rescorla-Wagner acquisition rule.

events.name: RUN_CS_ALONE
events.description: Learner ran a CS-alone trial, driving associative strength toward zero via the Rescorla-Wagner extinction rule.

events.name: RESET_TRIALS
events.description: Learner reset the trial history — associative strength, trial count, and phase all return to their starting values.

events.name: MEMORY_UPDATED
events.description: The memory state after each learner action — a composed listener (readout, grader) can subscribe; a harmless no-op when the atom runs standalone.
events.synonyms: forgetting curve, retention, memory decay, Ebbinghaus, spaced repetition

events.name: MODE_SELECTED
events.description: Lab router broadcast naming the active mode; this instrument renders when the mode equals matchMode, otherwise renders null.

events.name: ADD_REPETITION
events.description: Learner reviewed the material again — retention recovers a fraction of the forgotten gap (full boost spaced, half boost massed) and the decay clock restarts.

events.name: STEP_TIME
events.description: Advanced time by one twentieth of the horizon, decaying retention exponentially.

events.name: RESET
events.description: Learner reset the forgetting curve — retention, time, and repetition count return to their starting values.

events.name: OPERANT_UPDATED
events.description: The operant state after each learner action — a composed listener (readout, grader) can subscribe; a harmless no-op when the atom runs standalone.
events.synonyms: operant conditioning, reinforcement schedule, cumulative record, Skinner, scallop, instrumental conditioning

events.name: MODE_SELECTED
events.description: Lab router broadcast naming the active mode; this instrument renders when the mode equals matchMode, otherwise renders null.

events.name: EMIT_RESPONSE
events.description: Learner emitted a burst of responses (a lever-press batch); ratio schedules count the responses, interval schedules count the elapsed time, and either may make a reinforcer available.

events.name: DELIVER_REINFORCER
events.description: Learner collected the available reinforcer — a post-reinforcement pause flattens the cumulative record (the scallop) and variable schedules pick their next target.

events.name: SET_SCHEDULE
events.description: Learner switched the reinforcement schedule (fr, vr, fi, vi); progress toward the next reinforcer restarts.

events.name: RESET
events.description: Learner reset the cumulative record — responses, reinforcers, and elapsed time return to their starting values.

events.name: SIGNAL_UPDATED
events.description: The signal-detection state after each learner action — a composed listener (readout, grader) can subscribe; a harmless no-op when the atom runs standalone.
events.synonyms: signal detection, SDT, d prime, criterion, hit rate, false alarm, ROC point, sensitivity, response bias

events.name: MODE_SELECTED
events.description: Lab router broadcast naming the active mode; this instrument renders when the mode equals matchMode, otherwise renders null.

events.name: SET_CRITERION
events.description: Learner dragged the decision criterion; the theoretical hit and false-alarm rates recompute and the empirical counters re-anchor to zero.

events.name: RUN_TRIALS
events.description: Ran a batch of simulated detection trials at the configured base rate — each trial draws evidence from the noise or signal+noise distribution and scores a hit or false alarm against the criterion.

events.name: RESET
events.description: Learner reset the instrument — criterion, theoretical rates, and empirical counters return to their starting values.

events.name: STROOP_UPDATED
events.description: The Stroop scoring state after each learner action — a composed listener (readout, grader) can subscribe; a harmless no-op when the atom runs standalone.
events.synonyms: stroop, stroop effect, interference, incongruent trial, cognitive control, selective attention

events.name: MODE_SELECTED
events.description: Lab router broadcast naming the active mode; this instrument renders when the mode equals matchMode, otherwise renders null.

events.name: ANSWER_COLOR
events.description: Learner named the ink color of the current word; scored against the stimulus's inkName, bucketed by congruence.

events.name: NEXT_TRIAL
events.description: Advanced to the next stimulus, steered by congruentRatio: when the running congruent fraction exceeds the target, the next trial is drawn from the incongruent pool.

events.name: RESET
events.description: Learner reset the session — trial counters, accuracies, interference, and feedback return to their starting values.

events.description: A blank draft row persisted; the slug restamp follows.

events.name: WIKI_CREATED
events.description: A new page exists with its stable address; carries the id so the author lands in its editor.

events.name: WIKI_UPDATED
events.description: A page's content or metadata was written and the editing action is over — the open document refetches and version history snapshots on this.

events.name: WIKI_CONTENT_SAVED
events.description: An autosave landed while the author is still typing. Lists may refresh metadata; the open document must NOT refetch.

events.name: WIKI_DELETED
events.description: A page was removed.

events.name: PUBLISH_REQUESTED
events.description: A save that publishes was HELD, not written — the organism's approval circuit stores this payload on an ApprovalRequest and replays it through DO_PUBLISH_UPDATE when granted.
events.synonyms: held for review, publish requested, awaiting approval

events.name: PUBLISH_APPLY_FAILED
events.description: The approved payload could not be written (access denial, write failure). Route this to the approval gate's APPROVAL_REPLAY_FAILED so the request reopens.
events.synonyms: replay failed, publish failed after approval

events.name: WIKI_PUBLISH_APPLY_FAILED_INTERNAL
events.description: Internal failure hop from the replay persist.

events.name: DO_CREATE_DRAFT
events.description: Mint a new page with defaults only — document-first creation asks for nothing up front. parentId, when present, stamps the draft as a subpage.

events.name: DO_UPDATE
events.description: A page's content or metadata changed.

events.name: DO_PUBLISH_UPDATE
events.description: Replay an approval-granted publish payload through the writer; requestId rides along so a failure can reopen the right request.
events.synonyms: apply approved publish, replay held payload

events.name: DO_UPDATE_CONTENT
events.description: An autosave tick from the in-place editor: persist this partial content quietly.

events.name: DO_DELETE
events.description: Confirms a deletion request.

stages.description: A vast cloud of gas and dust collapses under its own gravity, and a protostar begins to glow at its center.
stages.label: Nebula

stages.description: Hydrogen fuses into helium in the core, and the star shines steadily for billions of years — this is where our Sun is now.
stages.label: Main Sequence

stages.description: The core runs out of hydrogen and contracts while the outer layers swell and cool into a huge red envelope.
stages.label: Red Giant

stages.description: The outer layers drift away as a planetary nebula, leaving behind a hot, dense stellar remnant that slowly cools and fades.
stages.label: White Dwarf

stages.description: A vast cloud of gas and dust collapses under its own gravity, forming a protostar far more massive than the Sun.
stages.label: Nebula

stages.description: The star burns through hydrogen far faster than a Sun-like star, shining bright blue-white.
stages.label: Main Sequence

stages.description: Heavier elements fuse in shells around an iron core, until fusion can no longer release energy.
stages.label: Red Supergiant

stages.description: The core collapses in an instant and rebounds, blasting the star's outer layers into space in a brilliant explosion.
stages.label: Supernova

stages.description: The crushed core survives as an ultra-dense sphere of neutrons, often spinning rapidly as a pulsar.
stages.label: Neutron Star

stages.description: A vast cloud of gas and dust collapses under its own gravity, forming an extremely massive protostar.
stages.label: Nebula

stages.description: The star burns its fuel at a furious rate, glowing intensely blue and living only a few million years.
stages.label: Main Sequence

stages.description: The star swells into an enormous, luminous supergiant while fusing progressively heavier elements in its core.
stages.label: Blue Supergiant

stages.description: The iron core collapses catastrophically and the star detonates, briefly outshining an entire galaxy.
stages.label: Supernova

stages.description: Gravity overwhelms every other force, and the collapsed core forms a black hole from which not even light can escape.
stages.label: Black Hole

default.caption: A phospholipid bilayer studded with proteins that forms the cell's outer boundary, enclosing everything you see here. It is selectively permeable, controlling which substances enter and leave.
default.name: Cell Membrane

default.caption: The cell's control center, enclosing most of its DNA within a double membrane. It directs growth and reproduction by regulating gene expression.
default.name: Nucleus

default.caption: A dense region inside the nucleus where ribosomal RNA is transcribed and ribosome subunits are assembled. Cells with high protein output have prominent nucleoli.
default.name: Nucleolus

default.caption: The powerhouse of the cell — its folded inner membrane hosts cellular respiration, converting nutrients into ATP. A typical animal cell carries hundreds.
default.name: Mitochondrion

default.caption: One of many mitochondria scattered through the cytosol; they cluster where energy demand is highest. Each carries its own small circular DNA.
default.name: Mitochondrion

default.caption: Mitochondria constantly divide and fuse, and damaged ones are recycled by lysosomes. Muscle cells pack thousands to sustain contraction.
default.name: Mitochondrion

default.caption: Flattened membrane sacs studded with ribosomes, continuous with the nuclear envelope. It folds and quality-checks proteins destined for secretion or membranes.
default.name: Rough ER

default.caption: Tubular membranes lacking ribosomes that synthesize lipids and steroids. It also detoxifies drugs and stores calcium ions for signaling.
default.name: Smooth ER

default.caption: A stack of flattened cisternae that modifies, sorts, and packages proteins arriving from the ER into vesicles — the cell's shipping department.
default.name: Golgi Apparatus

default.caption: Tiny RNA-protein machines that translate messenger RNA into polypeptide chains. They drift free in the cytosol or stud the rough ER.
default.name: Ribosomes

default.caption: A vesicle packed with hydrolytic enzymes that digest worn-out organelles and engulfed material. Its acidic interior keeps the enzymes safely contained.
default.name: Lysosome

default.caption: A pair of barrel-shaped microtubule arrays near the nucleus. They organize the spindle fibers that pull chromosomes apart during cell division.
default.name: Centrioles

default.caption: A small vesicle that breaks down fatty acids and neutralizes toxic hydrogen peroxide, converting it into water and oxygen.
default.name: Peroxisome

default.caption: Two polynucleotide strands wind around each other in a right-handed double helix, about ten base pairs per full turn. The rungs are the base pairs; the rails are the sugar-phosphate backbones.
default.name: Overall Helix

default.caption: Each rung pairs a purine with a pyrimidine: A with T (two hydrogen bonds) or G with C (three). Complementary pairing is what lets DNA copy itself faithfully.
default.name: One Base Pair

default.caption: The two outer rails are alternating deoxyribose sugars and phosphate groups, joined by phosphodiester bonds. The strands run antiparallel — one 5'→3', the other 3'→5'.
default.name: Sugar-Phosphate Backbone

default.caption: Because the two backbones are not exactly opposite each other, the helix has a wide major groove and a narrow minor groove. Transcription factors read base sequences mainly from the major groove.
default.name: Major & Minor Grooves

default.caption: Reactants: hydroxide (Nu⁻) and bromomethane. The C–Br bond is intact and the methyl group is tetrahedral — three H atoms umbrella away from bromine.
default.name: Reactants

default.caption: Approach: the nucleophile closes in from the backside — directly opposite the C–Br bond, along the σ* antibonding axis. Backside attack is what forces the inversion to come.
default.name: Backside Approach

default.caption: Transition state ‡: carbon is trigonal-bipyramidal — the Nu···C bond is half-formed and the C···Br bond half-broken (partial bonds drawn pale), and the three H atoms flatten into a plane perpendicular to the reaction axis.

default.caption: Products: the C–Br bond has broken and the Nu–C bond is fully formed. The hydrogen umbrella has flipped through the planar transition state — Walden inversion of configuration, the geometry 2D cannot show.
default.name: Products

default.caption: Departure: bromide, the leaving group, drifts away with the bonding electron pair; methanol stands with inverted geometry — the mirror-image arrangement of the reactant.
default.name: Departure

derivation.evidence: A determiner (Det) and a noun (N) combine into a Noun Phrase — here the subject "The cat".
A determiner (Det) and a noun (N) combine into a Noun Phrase — here the object "the mouse".
A verb (V) and its object Noun Phrase combine into a Verb Phrase — "chased the mouse".
The subject Noun Phrase and the Verb Phrase combine into the full Sentence.
A determiner (Det) and a noun (N) combine into a Noun Phrase — here the subject "A dog".
A determiner (Det) and a noun (N) combine into a Noun Phrase — here the object of the preposition, "the mat".
A preposition (P) and its Noun Phrase combine into a Prepositional Phrase — "on the mat".
A verb (V) and its Prepositional Phrase combine into a Verb Phrase — "sat on the mat".
The subject Noun Phrase and the Verb Phrase combine into the full Sentence.

derivation.evidence: A bare noun (N) alone forms a Noun Phrase — the subject "Birds".
A single intransitive verb (V) with no object still forms a Verb Phrase — "sing".

knobDefs.synonyms: AND gate, OR gate, NOT gate, XOR gate, conjunction, disjunction, negation, exclusive or, logic gate

knobDefs.label: Height
knobDefs.description: Canvas height in pixels.

knobDefs.label: Input Count
knobDefs.description: How many of each circuit's input pins get toggle buttons.

knobDefs.label: Match Mode
knobDefs.description: When composed behind a lab router, the MODE_SELECTED mode value this instrument responds to. Empty string means standalone — render immediately on INIT.

knobDefs.label: Show Intermediate Values
knobDefs.description: After propagation, label and color every gate with its computed value; when false only the output bulb is revealed.

knobDefs.label: Fallacy Set
knobDefs.description: The classification categories offered as pick buttons and drawn as the stacked backdrop tiers; value is the machine key, label and color are what the learner sees.
knobDefs.synonyms: fallacy, ad hominem, straw man, false dilemma, affirming the consequent, informal fallacy, valid argument

default.explanation: It attacks the person rather than the argument — ad hominem.
default.hint: Does this engage the plan, or the person?
default.text: You're only against the plan because you never liked me.

default.explanation: It presents two extremes as the only possibilities — false dilemma.
default.hint: Are those really the only two options?
default.text: We either ban all cars or accept choking smog forever.

default.explanation: From P→Q and Q it concludes P — affirming the consequent.
default.hint: Can the match be cancelled for another reason?
default.text: If it rains, the match is cancelled. The match is cancelled, so it rained.

default.explanation: It exaggerates the position into something easier to attack — straw man.
default.hint: Is that really what he argued?
default.text: He wants the library closed? Next he'll want books banned.

default.explanation: The conclusion follows necessarily from the premises — a valid argument.
default.hint: Does the conclusion follow from the premises?
default.text: All mammals breathe air. Whales are mammals, so whales breathe air.

knobDefs.label: Corpus
knobDefs.description: Argument cards (text, correct classification, hint, explanation) presented one at a time; category must be one of the categories values.
knobDefs.synonyms: argument card, corpus, exercise set, fallacy example, argument

knobDefs.label: Allow Model Edit
knobDefs.description: When true the learner can toggle object predicates to change the model; when false the toggle buttons render but edits are ignored.
knobDefs.synonyms: editable model, change the model, flip truth value

knobDefs.label: Domain
knobDefs.description: The finite domain of objects (position, label, and the predicate keys each object has); toggling a predicate on an object changes the model.
knobDefs.synonyms: domain of discourse, model, object, individual, universe of discourse

knobDefs.label: Height
knobDefs.description: Canvas height in pixels.

knobDefs.label: Match Mode
knobDefs.description: When composed behind a lab router, the MODE_SELECTED mode value this instrument responds to. Empty string means standalone — render immediately on INIT.

knobDefs.label: Predicates
knobDefs.description: The property vocabulary (key, label, ring color); each predicate an object has is drawn as a colored ring around it.
knobDefs.synonyms: predicate, property, unary relation, monadic predicate

knobDefs.label: Show Truth Values
knobDefs.description: After a statement is evaluated, show its computed T/F beside it.

knobDefs.label: Statements
knobDefs.description: Quantified statements evaluated against the model: FORALL px (every object has px), EXISTS px (some object has px), FORALL_EXISTS px py (if any object has px then some object has py).
knobDefs.synonyms: universal quantifier, existential quantifier, for all, there exists, quantified statement, predicate logic

knobDefs.label: Band Cues
knobDefs.description: Per-band cues for ESTIMATE_JUDGED — one row per error band (exact/close/off); bands with no row spawn nothing.

knobDefs.label: Celebration Cue
knobDefs.description: Cue spawned when a round completes (LEARN_ROUND_COMPLETE / TRACE_DONE).

knobDefs.label: Correct Cue
knobDefs.description: Cue spawned on a correct judged answer.

knobDefs.label: Progress Cue
knobDefs.description: Cue spawned on a partial arrangement check (some but not all slots correct).

knobDefs.label: Running
knobDefs.description: When false every cue arm is inert — visual feedback fully disabled without unmounting.

knobDefs.label: Streak Cue
knobDefs.description: Extra cue layered on the correct cue once the streak reaches the threshold.

knobDefs.label: Streak Threshold
knobDefs.description: Minimum ANSWER_JUDGED streak that adds the streak cue on top of the correct cue.

knobDefs.label: Verdict Cues
knobDefs.description: Per-verdict cues for CLASSIFY_UPDATED — one row per verdict string; verdicts with no row spawn nothing.

knobDefs.label: Wrong Cue
knobDefs.description: Cue spawned on a wrong judged answer (and an unmatched goal check).

knobDefs.label: First Term

knobDefs.label: Common Difference

knobDefs.label: Term Count

knobDefs.description: When composed behind a lab router, the MODE_SELECTED mode value this instrument responds to. Empty string means standalone — render immediately on INIT.

knobDefs.label: Vector Scale

knobDefs.label: Width

knobDefs.label: Height
knobDefs.description: Simulation height in pixels; bounds the wall box.

knobDefs.label: Show Velocity
knobDefs.description: Draw each body's velocity vector as an arrow.

knobDefs.label: Momentum Vector Scale
knobDefs.description: Length multiplier for the labeled momentum (p = m·v) vectors.

knobDefs.label: Velocity Scale
knobDefs.description: Length multiplier for the built-in velocity arrows.

knobDefs.label: Width
knobDefs.description: Simulation width in pixels; bounds the wall box.

knobDefs.label: Bodies

knobDefs.label: Damping
knobDefs.description: Fraction of velocity retained each substep (air resistance).

knobDefs.label: Gravity

knobDefs.label: Landing Threshold

knobDefs.label: Bodies
knobDefs.description: Initial conditions in scene cells: the star is static at the origin; each orbiter starts on the +x node with velocity tilted out of the equatorial plane — 0° (equatorial), ~45° (inclined, slightly elliptical), and 90° (polar) — so inclination and the line of nodes are visible.
knobDefs.synonyms: 3d, orbit, inclination, orbital plane, ascending node, apoapsis, periapsis, gravity, kepler, space

knobDefs.label: Camera
knobDefs.description: 3D camera pose; the view is user-rotatable, so azimuth only sets the starting angle on the orbital plane.

knobDefs.label: Gravitational Constant
knobDefs.description: Newton's G in scene-cell units; the central star's mass comes from its body entry, so acceleration is G·M/r².
knobDefs.synonyms: gravity, newton, inverse square, gravitational parameter

knobDefs.label: Post-processing
knobDefs.description: Post stack; bloom makes the emissive central star glow.

knobDefs.label: Show Velocity
knobDefs.description: Draw each body's 3D velocity vector as an arrow — watch it stay tangent to the inclined orbital plane.

knobDefs.label: Softening
knobDefs.description: Plummer softening length in cells added to r² — keeps a close periapsis pass from slingshotting a body to infinity.
knobDefs.synonyms: periapsis, close approach, singularity

knobDefs.label: Amplitude
knobDefs.description: Peak displacement of each source in scene cells; where two sources meet in phase the surface reinforces to twice this.
knobDefs.synonyms: interference, ripple, wavefront, superposition, diffraction, 3d

knobDefs.label: Camera
knobDefs.description: 3D camera pose; the view is user-rotatable, so azimuth only sets the starting angle over the surface.

knobDefs.label: Crest Color
knobDefs.description: Surface color band where displacement exceeds a quarter of the amplitude (crests).

knobDefs.label: Grid Size
knobDefs.description: Surface vertices per axis — the ripple surface is a gridSize×gridSize height field centered on the origin, so 9 gives the classic 9×9 tank.
knobDefs.synonyms: interference, ripple, wavefront, superposition, diffraction, 3d

knobDefs.label: Match Mode
knobDefs.description: When composed behind a lab router, the MODE_SELECTED mode value this instrument responds to. Empty string means standalone — render immediately on INIT.

knobDefs.label: Source Marker Color
knobDefs.description: Color of the small marker sphere drawn at each source's position.

knobDefs.label: Sources
knobDefs.description: One or two emitters. A point source radiates circular wavefronts from (x, y); a plane source treats x, y as a unit direction and emits straight wavefronts. Two point sources produce the classic interference pattern of nodal and antinodal lines.
knobDefs.synonyms: interference, ripple, wavefront, superposition, diffraction, 3d

knobDefs.label: Grid Spacing
knobDefs.description: Distance in scene cells between neighboring surface vertices along each axis.
knobDefs.synonyms: interference, ripple, wavefront, superposition, diffraction, 3d

knobDefs.label: Wave Speed
knobDefs.description: Phase speed in cells per simulated second; the angular frequency is ω = speed · k.
knobDefs.synonyms: interference, ripple, wavefront, superposition, diffraction, 3d

knobDefs.label: Surface Color
knobDefs.description: Surface color band near rest height, between crest and trough thresholds.

knobDefs.label: Trough Color
knobDefs.description: Surface color band where displacement drops below minus a quarter of the amplitude (troughs).

knobDefs.label: Velocity Scale
knobDefs.description: Length multiplier for the velocity arrows, when shown.

knobDefs.label: Wavelength
knobDefs.description: Distance between successive wavefronts in scene cells; sets the wavenumber k = 2π/λ.

knobDefs.description: 3D camera pose; the view is user-rotatable, so azimuth only sets the starting angle around the scene.

knobDefs.label: Charges

knobDefs.description: Coulomb's k in scene-cell units; each charge contributes E = k·q/r² along the sample−charge separation, superposed over the roster.

knobDefs.label: Force Scale
knobDefs.description: Length multiplier for the field arrows, in cells per unit field — tuned so a clamped arrow spans just under half a grid cell and arrows never overlap.

knobDefs.label: Grid Size
knobDefs.description: Samples per axis — the sampling volume is gridSize³ points centered on the origin, so 3 gives a 3×3×3 lattice of 27 field vectors.

knobDefs.label: Max Field
knobDefs.description: Arrow magnitude clamp in field units — near a charge the raw |E| blows up, so arrow lengths saturate at maxField while direction stays exact; the numeric readout always shows the unclamped vector. Also sets the low/mid/high magnitude color-band thresholds at 33%/66% of this value.

knobDefs.label: Presets
knobDefs.description: Named charge rosters cycled by the Next Preset button — a +/− dipole and two like positive charges, so the field's null point and repulsion geometry between like charges can be compared against the dipole.
knobDefs.synonyms: electric field, coulomb, dipole, field lines, vector field, 3d

knobDefs.label: Grid Spacing
knobDefs.description: Distance in scene cells between neighboring sample points along each axis.

knobDefs.label: Prior P(H)
knobDefs.description: Prior probability that the hypothesis is true before seeing evidence — the base rate.
knobDefs.synonyms: base rate, prior probability

knobDefs.label: Bins
knobDefs.description: Number of histogram buckets the sample means are counted into.

knobDefs.label: Draws Per Step
knobDefs.description: How many samples Draw Many adds to the means-histogram per click.

knobDefs.label: Match Mode
knobDefs.description: When composed behind a lab router, the MODE_SELECTED mode value this instrument responds to. Empty string means standalone — render immediately on INIT.

knobDefs.label: Population Kind
knobDefs.description: Shape of the population each sample is drawn from: uniform, skewed, or bimodal — the CLT normalizes the means-histogram regardless.
knobDefs.synonyms: population distribution, skewed distribution, bimodal, uniform distribution, sampling distribution, central limit theorem

knobDefs.label: Sample Size
knobDefs.description: Number of draws n per sample; larger n makes the means-histogram narrower and more normal.
knobDefs.synonyms: n, sample size, draws per sample

knobDefs.label: Show True Mean
knobDefs.description: Draw a guide line at the population mean.

knobDefs.label: True Mean
knobDefs.description: Population mean the sample means converge to; drawn as a guide line when Show True Mean is on.
knobDefs.synonyms: population mean, expected value, mu

knobDefs.label: Value Max
knobDefs.description: Population values range from 0 to this maximum.

knobDefs.label: Bias p
knobDefs.description: Probability of heads on each flip — shifts the histogram and the theoretical PMF.
knobDefs.synonyms: coin bias, success probability, binomial p, weighted coin

knobDefs.label: Convergence Threshold
knobDefs.description: Maximum |mean heads − theoretical mean| gap the narration will call converged, once at least 30 runs have accumulated.

knobDefs.label: Match Mode
knobDefs.description: When composed behind a lab router, the MODE_SELECTED mode value this instrument responds to. Empty string means standalone — render immediately on INIT.

knobDefs.label: Max Runs
knobDefs.description: Cap on accumulated trials; the run is done once reached, until Reset.

knobDefs.label: Runs Per Step
knobDefs.description: How many trials Run Many adds to the histogram per click.

knobDefs.label: Show Theoretical PMF
knobDefs.description: Overlay the binomial probability mass function, scaled to expected counts at the current run total, as markers the empirical histogram converges to.
knobDefs.synonyms: pmf, theoretical distribution, binomial distribution

knobDefs.label: Trials Per Run
knobDefs.description: Number of coin flips n per trial — the histogram x-axis runs from 0 to n heads.
knobDefs.synonyms: n, flips per trial, binomial n, number of trials

knobDefs.label: Confidence Level
knobDefs.description: Nominal confidence level — the long-run fraction of intervals that should capture the true mean.
knobDefs.synonyms: confidence level, coverage probability, 95 percent interval

knobDefs.label: Intervals Per Step
knobDefs.description: How many intervals Draw Many adds per click.

knobDefs.label: Match Mode
knobDefs.description: When composed behind a lab router, the MODE_SELECTED mode value this instrument responds to. Empty string means standalone — render immediately on INIT.

knobDefs.label: Max Rows
knobDefs.description: Row budget for the stacked intervals; the run is done once reached, until Reset.

knobDefs.label: Population SD
knobDefs.description: Standard deviation of the population each sample is drawn from — sets interval width together with n, and the canvas's x domain (true mean ± 3 SD).
knobDefs.synonyms: standard deviation, sigma, spread

knobDefs.label: Sample Size
knobDefs.description: Number of draws n per sample; larger n makes every interval narrower.
knobDefs.synonyms: n, sample size, draws per sample

knobDefs.label: True Mean
knobDefs.description: Population mean the intervals try to capture; drawn as the dark vertical guide line.
knobDefs.synonyms: population mean, mu, true value

knobDefs.label: Match Mode
knobDefs.description: When composed behind a lab router, the MODE_SELECTED mode value this instrument responds to. Empty string means standalone — render immediately on INIT.

knobDefs.label: Mean
knobDefs.description: Initial center of the distribution; learners move it with the mean slider.
knobDefs.synonyms: mu, average, center

knobDefs.label: Presets
knobDefs.description: Named mean/standard-deviation combinations the Step button and transport clock cycle through.
knobDefs.synonyms: preset, roster, shape, scenario

knobDefs.label: Standard Deviation
knobDefs.description: Initial spread of the distribution; learners move it with the spread slider.
knobDefs.synonyms: sigma, spread, standard deviation

knobDefs.label: Y Max
knobDefs.description: Minimum top of the y axis; the canvas grows above it automatically when a small standard deviation pushes the peak higher.

knobDefs.label: Mode
knobDefs.description: Which psychology simulation to render: classical (Pavlovian) conditioning trials, or the Maslow's-hierarchy-of-needs scenario classifier.
knobDefs.synonyms: psychology, classical conditioning, Pavlovian conditioning, Pavlov, Pavlov's dog, stimulus, conditioned stimulus, unconditioned stimulus, conditioned response, unconditioned response, acquisition, extinction, Rescorla-Wagner, associative strength, associative learning, Maslow, Maslow's hierarchy, hierarchy of needs, needs pyramid, motivation, self-actualization, esteem needs, love and belonging, safety needs, physiological needs

knobDefs.label: Learning Rate (α)
knobDefs.description: Rescorla-Wagner learning-rate parameter — the fraction of the prediction error (λ − V, or 0 − V during extinction) applied to associative strength on each trial.
knobDefs.synonyms: alpha, learning rate, Rescorla-Wagner alpha, salience, associability

knobDefs.label: Curve Color
knobDefs.description: Color of the acquisition/extinction curve polyline and its current-value marker.

knobDefs.label: History Cap
knobDefs.description: Maximum number of sampled associative-strength points kept in the acquisition/extinction curve history; older points are dropped once this is exceeded.
knobDefs.synonyms: history length, curve window, sample cap

knobDefs.label: Asymptote (λ)
knobDefs.description: Maximum associative strength the unconditioned stimulus supports; RUN_PAIRING drives V toward this value, RUN_CS_ALONE (extinction) drives V toward 0.
knobDefs.synonyms: lambda, asymptote, maximum associative strength, US intensity, unconditioned stimulus intensity

knobDefs.label: Match Mode
knobDefs.description: When composed behind a lab router, the MODE_SELECTED mode value this instrument responds to. Empty string means standalone — render immediately on INIT.

knobDefs.label: Title
knobDefs.description: Title shown above the canvas.

knobDefs.label: Advance Button Label
knobDefs.description: Label text for the button that advances to the next item.

knobDefs.label: Auto-Advance Interval (ms)
knobDefs.description: Milliseconds between automatic advances while running — the 32ms base tick accumulates elapsed time and fires ADVANCE each time this interval elapses.

knobDefs.label: Auto Run
knobDefs.description: When true the advance clock starts on load and the drill flips to the next item every advanceMs milliseconds; toggle live with the Auto/Pause button.

knobDefs.label: Categories
knobDefs.description: Ordered bottom-to-top roster of category buckets (value/label/color) used to render the stacked backdrop and the pick buttons; order determines the backdrop's stacking, widest at the bottom to narrowest at the top.
knobDefs.synonyms: category, bucket, class, tier, level, classification, roster

knobDefs.label: Correct Highlight Color
knobDefs.description: Fill color for the correct category once the learner has picked.

knobDefs.label: Incorrect Highlight Color
knobDefs.description: Fill color for the learner's picked category when it does not match the correct category.

default.text: Grabbing a granola bar because you haven't eaten anything since breakfast yesterday.
Stocking the pantry with canned goods before a winter storm hits.
Installing a deadbolt lock after a break-in two doors down.
Negotiating a long-term contract instead of freelance gigs, for steady income.
Joining a weekly book club to make new friends in a new city.
Calling an old friend just to catch up and feel connected.
Working extra hours to earn the promotion and the recognition that comes with it.
Entering a competition to prove your skill to your peers.
Taking a sabbatical to finally write the novel you've always wanted to write.
Learning a new instrument purely for the joy of mastering it.

knobDefs.label: Items
knobDefs.description: Roster of items the learner classifies; each carries its prompt text, the value of its correct category, and optional hint/explanation text shown before/after the pick.
knobDefs.synonyms: item, prompt, scenario, situation, case, example, question

knobDefs.label: Loop Round
knobDefs.description: When true the item cursor wraps past the last item forever (a looping drill) instead of ending the round at the summary screen.

knobDefs.label: Match Mode
knobDefs.description: When composed behind a lab router, the MODE_SELECTED mode value this instrument responds to. Empty string means standalone — render immediately on INIT.

knobDefs.label: Order Stride
knobDefs.description: Items advance by this stride through the roster — 1 is sequential; a stride coprime with the roster length (e.g. 3) interleaves the corpus so adjacent items differ.

knobDefs.label: Pass Score

knobDefs.label: Penalty Per Miss
knobDefs.description: Rubric points subtracted for each incorrect pick (score never drops below 0).

knobDefs.label: Points Per Correct
knobDefs.description: Rubric points added to the score for each correct pick; at the default 1 with no penalty, the plain correct/attempted counts render instead of the rubric score.

knobDefs.label: Retry Button Label
knobDefs.description: Label text for the button that restarts the round from the end-of-round summary.

knobDefs.label: Score Cap
knobDefs.description: Upper bound on the rubric score; 0 means uncapped.

knobDefs.label: Show Hint
knobDefs.description: Show each item's hint line beneath the prompt before the learner picks; hide for a harder drill.

knobDefs.description: Height of the stacked bar, in pixels.

knobDefs.label: Bar Margin
knobDefs.description: Horizontal margin, in pixels, on each side of the stacked bar.

knobDefs.label: Concentration Rate
knobDefs.description: Fraction of an inner stratum's (upper-middle/working) share pulled outward to the adjacent extreme stratum per generation, scaled by (1 - mobility/100) — the low-mobility 'rich stay rich, poor stay poor' term. Keep this and Mobility Rate each ≤ 1.0 so shares always stay non-negative.
knobDefs.synonyms: social mobility, intergenerational mobility, mobility index, class mobility, income inequality

knobDefs.label: Income Weights
knobDefs.description: Relative income multiplier for each of the five strata, index-aligned with Strata (same order: richest to poorest). Used with the current shares to compute the Gini-style inequality index: income_i = share_i × weight_i, normalized into income shares, then the discrete Gini formula over cumulative population vs. cumulative income (poorest to richest).
knobDefs.synonyms: income distribution, income inequality, Gini index, Gini coefficient, wealth gap, economic inequality

knobDefs.label: Initial Mobility Index
knobDefs.description: Starting value (0-100) of the mobility index.
knobDefs.synonyms: social mobility, intergenerational mobility, mobility index, class mobility

knobDefs.label: Match Mode
knobDefs.description: When composed behind a lab router, the MODE_SELECTED mode value this instrument responds to. Empty string means standalone — render immediately on INIT.

knobDefs.label: Mobility Rate
knobDefs.description: Fraction of a non-middle stratum's share that migrates one step toward the middle class per generation, scaled by the mobility index (mobilityFrac = mobility/100). Keep this and Concentration Rate each ≤ 1.0 so shares always stay non-negative.
knobDefs.synonyms: social mobility, intergenerational mobility, mobility index, class mobility

knobDefs.label: Strata
knobDefs.description: The five class strata, richest to poorest, each with its starting population share (must sum to 100) and bar color. Drives the stacked bar; the mobility transition and Gini index are computed over these five shares in fixed order.
knobDefs.synonyms: social class, class strata, class structure, upper class, upper-middle class, middle class, working class, lower class, socioeconomic status

default.explanation: C. Wright Mills: one person out of work is a personal trouble to be solved by that person's character and skills. When millions are out of work at once because factories close and whole job categories are automated away, the job market itself has broken down — that's a public issue rooted in economic structure, not individual failing.

options.label: He just isn't trying hard enough to get hired.
Structural unemployment — factories closing and jobs being automated away are eliminating entire categories of work across the economy.
Employers today are only looking for young talent.

default.troubleText: I can't find a job no matter how hard I try — it must be something wrong with me.

default.explanation: When only a few marriages fail, look to the couple. When divorce rates climb across an entire society within the same few years, the institution of marriage itself is under structural strain — a public issue, not a private failing.

options.label: A generation-wide collapse of the economic and social supports that used to hold marriages together.
She should have picked a better partner.
Marriage counseling just doesn't work anymore.

default.troubleText: My marriage is falling apart, and it feels like it's entirely my fault.

default.explanation: One student in debt is a private trouble. A whole generation carrying record debt loads, at the same time public funding for education has been withdrawn, is a public issue built into how college gets paid for.

options.label: He shouldn't have gone to such an expensive school.
People today just don't budget carefully enough.
A structural shift that moved the cost of higher education from public funding onto individual borrowers, across an entire generation.

default.troubleText: I'm drowning in student debt and can't seem to get ahead, no matter what I do.

default.explanation: A single burned-out worker is a personal trouble. When burnout tracks a structural shift toward insecure, boundary-less work across millions of workers at once, it's a public issue in how work itself has been reorganized.

options.label: She needs to manage her stress better.
An economy-wide shift toward precarious, always-on gig and contract work that has eroded job security for millions.
Some people just aren't cut out for a demanding career.

default.troubleText: I feel completely burned out and anxious all the time at work, and I don't know why I can't handle it like everyone else.

knobDefs.synonyms: sociological imagination, C. Wright Mills, Mills, personal trouble, public issue, biography and history, private trouble, structural issue

knobDefs.label: Art Style

knobDefs.label: Material Recipes
knobDefs.description: How each named material renders, as a data-driven `draw-mesh` `material` preset resolved against the chosen palette's steps (a color reference like magic's `emissive: 'highlight'` names a palette step, not a literal hex): PBR kind (standard | physical | toon | basic) plus its knobs — metalness/roughness for metal, transmission/ior for crystal glass, an emissive-driven glow for magic, flatShading for stone's faceted low-poly look, and an outline width for toon's inverted-hull line.

knobDefs.label: Motion Timing
knobDefs.description: Animation personality: loop durations per anim state, one-shot (death/collapse) duration, flame-flicker cycle, idle/walk bob amplitude in cell units, and the full-turn spin constant. Loop keyframes must start and end on the same values.

knobDefs.label: Color Palettes
knobDefs.description: Master 5-step value scales plus drop-shadow RGBA strings per palette kind.

knobDefs.label: Post Presets
knobDefs.description: Per-style post-process preset — bloom ({ intensity, threshold, smoothing }) and vignette ({ offset, darkness }) — applied only where the style calls for it; neon leans on both for its glow, every other style ships empty (post stays off by default).

knobDefs.label: Proportion Grid
knobDefs.description: The 0..1 cell-box grid every asset sits on: feet/base end at groundLine, the ground drop shadow is an ellipse at shadowBand, unit body mass centers at bodyCenterY, heads read large (headRatio of body height — chibi readability), and an asset never exceeds maxLayers draw layers.

knobDefs.label: Lighting Rig
knobDefs.description: Per-style lighting preset shaped like the canvas `lighting` prop: ambient (flat fill light), directional (the shaped key light + its `position` in cells), hemisphere (sky/ground bounce tint), and an environment preset name ('room' | 'none') for PBR reflections. Style branches read here instead of hardcoding lights — glossy and low-poly run the full room rig, flat/cartoon/neon drop the environment and dial the directional key down or up for their look.

knobDefs.label: Shape Language
knobDefs.description: Personality → geometry mapping (circles read friendly, squares stable, triangles dangerous): pick the dominant shape family per roster role before authoring. Round = ellipses + soft curves; angular = triangles + sharp path corners; square = rects + flat tops; radial = concentric ellipses.

knobDefs.label: Style Direction
knobDefs.description: The theme direction token for the whole 3D art bible — the recipe branch every material/mesh molecule renders the same geometry+palette through: glossy PBR house style (metalness/roughness + a room environment + a soft directional key), pure minimal flat (basic unlit fills, weak directional, no environment), heavy-outline cartoon (bright ambient + an inverted-hull toon outline), neon (dim ambient, bloom + vignette post, emissive-driven materials), or low-poly (glossy's rig with `flatShading` + low `segments` — in 3D low-poly IS a style token like every other direction, not a geometry rewrite, unlike its 2D twin where every style shares one silhouette). One flip restyles every material-composed mesh; generated authoring preambles interpolate it.

knobDefs.label: Store before-and-after snapshots?
knobDefs.description: Store a full before-and-after snapshot of each change. More detail, but a larger audit log.
knobDefs.synonyms: before after, snapshot, diff, change snapshot, field diff

knobDefs.label: Entity to audit
knobDefs.description: Type name of the entity whose mutations get logged

knobDefs.label: Event-kind filter
knobDefs.description: When set, only these kinds are audited: the payload's `kind` field, or the delivering event's name when there is no kind. Empty list = capture every event.

knobDefs.label: Track every change
knobDefs.description: Keep an audit trail of every change to records — who changed what, and when. Off by default.
knobDefs.synonyms: enable, turn on, enforce, require, activate, apply, switch on, audit, audit trail, log changes, track changes, who edited what, mutation log, change history, edit history, modification log, accountability log, record changes, log every edit, compliance log

knobDefs.label: Skip fields
knobDefs.description: Entity fields to omit from the before/after snapshots — e.g. passwords or other sensitive fields you do not want copied into the audit trail.

knobDefs.label: How long should the audit log be kept (days)?
knobDefs.description: Number of days to retain audit entries. Default 2555 ≈ 7 years, typical for compliance.
knobDefs.synonyms: log retention, keep for, audit expiry, retention period, log lifetime

knobDefs.label: Calendar id
knobDefs.description: Google calendar to sync with; blank = the service's default (GOOGLE_CALENDAR_ID env, else primary).
knobDefs.synonyms: google calendar id, target calendar

knobDefs.label: Description field
knobDefs.description: Target-entity field holding the description/notes; blank = none.
knobDefs.synonyms: notes field, details field

knobDefs.label: Duration field
knobDefs.description: Target-entity field holding the per-row duration in minutes (e.g. ClassSession.durationMinutes). Takes precedence over the fixed `durationMinutes` when set; ignored when `endField` is set. Field precedence: endField > durationField > durationMinutes — the corpus carries all these event shapes.
knobDefs.synonyms: minutes field, length field, per-row duration

knobDefs.label: Duration (minutes)
knobDefs.description: Fixed event length used when both `endField` and `durationField` are blank; the calendar service computes the timezone-correct end.
knobDefs.synonyms: length, event duration, minutes

knobDefs.label: Sync with Google Calendar
knobDefs.description: Push local records to Google Calendar and pull remote events into the CalendarEvent store. Off by default; needs the calendar service credentials (GOOGLE_CALENDAR_SA_KEY).
knobDefs.synonyms: enable, calendar sync, google calendar, two-way sync, sync events, connect calendar

knobDefs.label: End field
knobDefs.description: Target-entity field holding the ISO end. Blank = derive the end from `durationMinutes` instead (the corpus carries all four event shapes).
knobDefs.synonyms: end date field, finishes field

knobDefs.label: Location field
knobDefs.description: Target-entity field holding the location; blank = none.
knobDefs.synonyms: place field, venue field

knobDefs.label: Start field
knobDefs.description: Target-entity field holding the ISO start (dateTime, or YYYY-MM-DD for all-day).
knobDefs.synonyms: start date field, begins field, scheduledAt field

knobDefs.label: Entity to push
knobDefs.description: Event-shaped entity whose rows export to Google Calendar. MUST declare the marker columns `externalEventId : string = ""` and `syncedAt : number = 0` (stamped by the push loop). Defaults to the atom's own CalendarEvent store so the standalone validates; rebind per composition.
knobDefs.synonyms: entity to sync, source entity, record type, appointments entity, sessions entity

knobDefs.label: Title field
knobDefs.description: Target-entity field holding the event title.
knobDefs.synonyms: summary field, name field

knobDefs.label: Agenda group-by field
knobDefs.description: Row field the agenda list groups its day sections by. Rebound hosts point this at their own timestamp column (e.g. startTime, scheduledAt).
knobDefs.synonyms: group field, section field, day field

knobDefs.label: Agenda item actions
knobDefs.description: Per-item action buttons on agenda-list rows — data-list itemActions descriptors (label/event/icon/variant). Consumers override to wire their own row actions (View/Edit/Delete) so agenda hosts never need a second table for actions.
knobDefs.synonyms: agenda actions, row actions, event actions, list actions

knobDefs.label: Agenda list body content tree
knobDefs.description: Render-ui SExpr for calendarLook='agenda-list' — events grouped by day with overline day headers (Today, Tomorrow, …) and a time marker per event.

knobDefs.label: Badge binding
knobDefs.description: Per-row binding for the event status/badge slot.

knobDefs.label: Body content tree
knobDefs.description: Render-ui SExpr rendered after events load for calendarLook='month' — the month-grid + upcoming-events list. calendarLook='agenda-list' / 'week-timeline' render agendaListBodyContent / weekTimelineBodyContent instead; all three share this trait's state machine, emits, and listens.

knobDefs.label: Show the calendar's own search box?
knobDefs.description: Embeds a title search box in the toolbar above the calendar body (all three calendarLook trees). Defaults false: std-calendar has never had a search box, so an untouched consumer's surface is unchanged; the primary path is composing std-search beside this atom and wiring XSearch.SEARCH -> REFETCH_QUERY. Set true only for a standalone calendar with no page-level search affordance.
knobDefs.synonyms: inline search, calendar search, built-in search, show search, duplicate search

knobDefs.label: Calendar look
knobDefs.description: Layer 3 body layout: default month-grid + upcoming-events list ('month'), day-grouped agenda list ('agenda-list'), or 7-column week timeline ('week-timeline').

knobDefs.label: Description binding
knobDefs.description: Per-row binding for the event description slot.

knobDefs.label: Upcoming-events columns
knobDefs.description: Row field descriptors for the 'Upcoming Events' data-list under calendarLook='month'. Rebound hosts must override this — it is a literal entity[field.name] lookup, unlike titleBinding/timeBinding/descriptionBinding (expression bindings), so it does not follow a rebind automatically.
knobDefs.synonyms: upcoming events columns, month view fields, event list columns

knobDefs.label: Filter bar look
knobDefs.description: Visual treatment for the embedded filter bar, mirroring std-filter's own enum. Only applies when `filters` is non-empty.
knobDefs.synonyms: filter bar style, facet style, chips, pills

knobDefs.label: Which filters should appear above the calendar?
knobDefs.description: Dropdown filter facets by field, rendered as an embedded filter bar above the calendar body (all three calendarLook trees); each selection fires REFETCH_FILTER on this trait. Empty (the default) = no filter bar, which is the right setting whenever the page already composes std-filter beside this calendar and routes XFilter.FILTER -> REFETCH_FILTER — that is the wired owner and remains the primary path. Use this knob only for a standalone calendar with no page-level filter affordance.
knobDefs.synonyms: filter bar, faceted filters, field filters, dropdowns

knobDefs.label: Which relation fields to hydrate?
knobDefs.description: Entity relation field names to hydrate on fetch (e.g. a `category : Category` field named `category`), so chip bindings can use dot-paths like @item.category.name. Empty = no hydration, the default.
knobDefs.synonyms: relation hydration, populate relations, joined fields, hydrate relations

knobDefs.label: On Event Click
knobDefs.description: Event emitted when a calendar chip is clicked: UI:{onEventClick} with { event } carrying the clicked row. Empty means chips are not clickable.
knobDefs.synonyms: open event, event click, select event, chip click

knobDefs.label: Which column does the search box match against?
knobDefs.description: Name the field on this entity the search box's str/includes filter matches against. Declared, never inferred: an entity with no `name` column must set this to a real field (e.g. title, description) or the search box can never match a row.
knobDefs.synonyms: search column, search on field, match field, search key

knobDefs.label: Search box placeholder text
knobDefs.description: Hint text inside the calendar's search box (e.g. 'Search events…').
knobDefs.synonyms: search hint, placeholder, search box text, search label

knobDefs.label: Start field
knobDefs.description: Row column holding the timestamp the calendar grid places each chip by. Rebound hosts point this at their own column (e.g. startTime, startsAt, dueAt); the chip's LABEL comes from titleBinding, not from here.
knobDefs.synonyms: start column, date column, when field, timestamp field

knobDefs.label: Body content tree
knobDefs.description: Render-ui SExpr rendered after rows load when browseLook = table (the default). Toolbar (search when bodySearch, filter bar when filters is non-empty) above the canonical data-grid call. Until 2026-08-27 this was the only one of the six looks with no search affordance at all. See denseBodyContent/feedBodyContent/galleryBodyContent for the other browseLook bodies; any may be overridden directly while inheriting the same trait, state machine, emits, and listens. Inlined directly (not via a composed sibling trait) 2026-09-08 — a separately-listening DataGrid1 sibling fired unconditionally on every BrowseItemLoaded regardless of browseLook, racing the correct body for slot main (a listens guard can't gate this: both the Rust interpreter and the TS codegen path restrict a listens guard's context to @payload only, so a browseLook config check there always evaluates undefined).

Selecting a non-table look swaps which body tree renders after rows load; any body may still be overridden directly at the call site for a one-off layout.

knobDefs.label: Which field does the first load filter on?
knobDefs.description: Name the field the INITIAL load filters on, paired with initialFilterValue. This is the detail half of a list-detail pair: a thread that must wait for a conversation to be picked sets the field to its parent key and leaves the value blank, so the first load matches nothing and the empty state shows instead of every record in the table. REFETCH_FILTER then supplies the real selection. Left blank the first load is unfiltered, which is the default.
knobDefs.synonyms: initial filter, first load filter, wait for selection, detail pane filter, requires selection, start empty

knobDefs.label: What value does the first load filter for?
knobDefs.description: The value initialFilterField must equal on the first load. Blank is meaningful: it matches only records whose field is itself blank, which for a detail pane is normally none — that is how a thread stays empty until its parent is selected.
knobDefs.synonyms: initial filter value, first load value, default selection
