knobDefs.description: Event emitted when the user runs a global search

knobDefs.label: Idle content
knobDefs.description: The normal content view (e.g. the data ledger/browse trait) shown when no search is active.

knobDefs.label: Result columns
knobDefs.description: Columns shown in the search-results grid; maps entity fields to display cells.

knobDefs.label: Results title
knobDefs.description: Heading shown above the search-results grid.

knobDefs.label: Search field
knobDefs.description: Entity field matched against the query (case-insensitive substring).

knobDefs.label: Which fields appear in the record panel?
knobDefs.description: Each entry maps one entity field to a labelled row in the panel. Unlike a list row, a detail panel SHOULD label every field — the value stands alone here with no column header or repeated row position to name it.
knobDefs.synonyms: detail fields, record fields, panel fields, shown fields

knobDefs.label: Which field is the record's title?
knobDefs.description: Name of the field on the loaded record shown as the panel title (e.g. contactName, subject, title).
knobDefs.synonyms: title field, heading field, name field, label field

knobDefs.label: Which fields appear in the form?
knobDefs.description: Entity fields rendered as inputs inside the modal form.
knobDefs.synonyms: form fields, inputs, editable fields, field list

knobDefs.label: Trigger events
knobDefs.description: Event names that should fire a notification. Set this to the upstream event name (e.g. OrderPlaced, CheckoutCompleted) so this atom listens for events from the orbital that emits them. The orbital owning this trait reacts whenever the named event fires anywhere in the schema.
knobDefs.synonyms: subscribe to event, listen for event, react to event, watch for, wire upstream event, observe event from another orbital, cross-orbital subscription, on-event trigger

knobDefs.label: Severity
knobDefs.description: info, success, warning, or error — controls styling
knobDefs.synonyms: alert level, priority, urgency

knobDefs.label: Message template
knobDefs.description: Text shown to the recipient; supports payload interpolation
knobDefs.synonyms: notification text, message body, alert text

knobDefs.label: Name
knobDefs.description: Icon name as string (resolved from iconMap)

knobDefs.label: Content
knobDefs.description: Text content (alternative to children)

knobDefs.label: Label
knobDefs.description: Button label text (alternative to children for schema-driven rendering)

knobDefs.label: Metrics
knobDefs.description: One stat card per entry; declares aggregation, format, and styling
knobDefs.synonyms: list of KPI cards / stat tiles / metric cards. each entry has label / value / format / icon / variant / aggregation. user phrases: 'replace metrics with X, Y, Z' -> rewrite array; 'add Revenue tile' -> append entry; 'change KPIs to X' -> rewrite array

knobDefs.label: Stats look
knobDefs.description: Layer 3 body layout: default per-metric stat-card grid ('cards'), Stripe-dashboard KPI tile row ('kpi-tiles'), single oversize hero number ('hero-metric'), or chart-first sparkline tile grid ('sparkline-row').

knobDefs.label: Section title
knobDefs.description: Heading shown above the stat-card grid
knobDefs.synonyms: the section header text. user phrases: 'rename section to X' / 'title the KPIs X' / 'change section title to X' -> X

knobDefs.label: Group / categorize / bucket / split by field
knobDefs.description: Entity field whose values become the chart's category buckets. Set this when the user voices 'group by X' / 'categorize by X' / 'bucket by X' / 'split by X' / 'break down by X' for any non-time field X (for time-units, set period + timeAxis=true instead).
knobDefs.synonyms: regroup / rebucket / categorize / breakdown by / split by / segment by. user phrases: 'group by status' -> categoryField=status; 'group by region' / 'by region' -> categoryField=region; 'group by category' / 'by category' -> categoryField=category; 'group by product' / 'by product' -> categoryField=product; 'group by month' / 'by month' -> categoryField=month (when explicitly requested as a category, not a time bucket); 'split by X' / 'break down by X' / 'segment by X' / 'bucket by X' -> categoryField=X

knobDefs.label: Subtitle
knobDefs.description: Secondary line below the title
knobDefs.synonyms: secondary header below the title. user phrases: 'with subtitle X' / 'set subtitle to X' -> X

knobDefs.label: Title
knobDefs.description: Heading shown above the chart
knobDefs.synonyms: the chart's header text. user phrases: 'rename to X' / 'title it X' / 'change the title to X' / 'call it X' -> X

knobDefs.label: Value field
knobDefs.description: Numeric field aggregated per bucket (blank = row count)
knobDefs.synonyms: the numeric column to aggregate. empty string counts rows. user phrases: 'sum revenue' -> valueField=revenue + aggregation=sum

knobDefs.description: Recipient used when `recipients` is empty, instead of the acting user. The acting-user fallback (used when this is blank) is intended for personal notifications only — set this to an ops/team address (e.g. 'ops@example.com') for system alerts like low-stock or shipping notices, so the acting user isn't notified in place of the intended audience.
knobDefs.synonyms: default recipient, backup recipient, ops address, fallback address, notify default, alert owner

knobDefs.label: Guard comparison
knobDefs.description: How to gate dispatch. `eq` (default) does string-equality via `triggerStatus` against the upstream event's `status` field, exactly as before. `gt`/`lt`/`gte`/`lte` instead numerically compare `guardField` (read from the event's `data` payload) against `guardValue` — e.g. fire only when a stock level drops below a threshold.
knobDefs.synonyms: comparison operator, threshold operator, guard mode, trigger comparison, numeric gate, greater than, less than, threshold crossing

knobDefs.label: Message template
knobDefs.description: Text shown to the recipient; supports payload interpolation
knobDefs.synonyms: notification text, message body, alert text

knobDefs.label: Trigger status
knobDefs.description: When `guardOp` is `eq` and this is set, dispatch only when the upstream event's `status` field equals this value (e.g. fire only when a record becomes 'approved'). Empty = fire on every subscribed event. Ignored when `guardOp` is a numeric comparison.
knobDefs.synonyms: on status, when status, status filter, only when, fire on, react on status

knobDefs.label: Modal title
knobDefs.description: Heading shown at the top of the confirmation modal

knobDefs.label: Event key for preferences
knobDefs.description: Stable key naming the upstream event this listener is bound to (e.g. 'OrderPlaced'). NotificationPreference rows (std-notification-center) whose eventKey equals this key — or is blank — apply to this listener's dispatches.
knobDefs.synonyms: preference key, event name, subscription key, notification topic

knobDefs.label: Message template
knobDefs.description: Text shown to the recipient; supports payload interpolation
knobDefs.synonyms: notification text, message body, alert text

knobDefs.label: Message template
knobDefs.description: Text shown to the recipient; supports payload interpolation
knobDefs.synonyms: notification text, message body, alert text

knobDefs.label: Trigger status
knobDefs.description: When `guardOp` is `eq` and this is set, dispatch only when the upstream event's `status` field equals this value (e.g. fire only when a record becomes 'approved'). Empty = fire on every subscribed event. Ignored when `guardOp` is a numeric comparison.
knobDefs.synonyms: on status, when status, status filter, only when, fire on, react on status

knobDefs.label: Calendar id
knobDefs.description: Google calendar to sync with; blank = the service's default (GOOGLE_CALENDAR_ID env, else primary).
knobDefs.synonyms: google calendar id, target calendar

knobDefs.label: Description field
knobDefs.description: Target-entity field holding the description/notes; blank = none.
knobDefs.synonyms: notes field, details field

knobDefs.label: Sync with Google Calendar
knobDefs.description: Push local records to Google Calendar and pull remote events into the CalendarEvent store. Off by default; needs the calendar service credentials (GOOGLE_CALENDAR_SA_KEY).
knobDefs.synonyms: enable, calendar sync, google calendar, two-way sync, sync events, connect calendar

knobDefs.label: End field
knobDefs.description: Target-entity field holding the ISO end. Blank = derive the end from `durationMinutes` instead (the corpus carries all four event shapes).
knobDefs.synonyms: end date field, finishes field

knobDefs.label: Start field
knobDefs.description: Target-entity field holding the ISO start (dateTime, or YYYY-MM-DD for all-day).
knobDefs.synonyms: start date field, begins field, scheduledAt field

knobDefs.label: Entity to push
knobDefs.description: Event-shaped entity whose rows export to Google Calendar. MUST declare the marker columns `externalEventId : string = ""` and `syncedAt : number = 0` (stamped by the push loop). Defaults to the atom's own CalendarEvent store so the standalone validates; rebind per composition.
knobDefs.synonyms: entity to sync, source entity, record type, appointments entity, sessions entity

knobDefs.label: Title field
knobDefs.description: Target-entity field holding the event title.
knobDefs.synonyms: summary field, name field

knobDefs.label: Idle content
knobDefs.description: The normal content view (e.g. the data ledger/browse trait) shown when no search is active.

knobDefs.label: Result columns
knobDefs.description: Columns shown in the search-results grid; maps entity fields to display cells.

knobDefs.label: Results title
knobDefs.description: Heading shown above the search-results grid.

knobDefs.label: Label
knobDefs.description: Button label text (alternative to children for schema-driven rendering)

knobDefs.label: Categories
knobDefs.description: The two-way classification ladder: allophones of one phoneme (complementary distribution, no meaning contrast) versus separate phonemes (a minimal pair contrasts meaning in an identical environment).
knobDefs.synonyms: phoneme, allophone, complementary distribution, minimal pair, contrast, phonology

default.explanation: A minimal pair (sip/zip) proves [s] and [z] contrast in identical environments and change meaning — they are separate phonemes /s/ and /z/.
default.hint: Environments to consider: word-initial, between vowels, after a nasal, word-final. Features — [s]: +consonantal, −voice, +coronal, +strident. [z]: +consonantal, +voice, +coronal, +strident.
default.text:
English [s] and [z] — are [s] and [z] separate phonemes or allophones of one phoneme?

Evidence:
- sip [sɪp]  vs  zip [zɪp] — same environment, meaning changes
- seal [siːl]  vs  zeal [ziːl] — same environment, meaning changes
- A minimal pair exists: swapping [s] for [z] makes a different word.

default.explanation: Clear [l] and dark [ɫ] stand in complementary distribution — [l] in onsets, [ɫ] in codas — so they are allophones of one phoneme /l/.
default.hint: Environments to consider: word-initial, between vowels, after a nasal, word-final. Features — [l]: +consonantal, +voice, +lateral, −velarized. [ɫ]: +consonantal, +voice, +lateral, +velarized.
default.text:
English clear [l] and dark [ɫ] — are [l] and [ɫ] separate phonemes or allophones of one phoneme?

Evidence:
- leaf [liːf] — clear [l] only before a vowel
- feel [fiːɫ] — dark [ɫ] only word-finally after a vowel
- No minimal pair exists: the two sounds never occur in the same environment.

default.explanation: Stop [d] appears after pauses and nasals, fricative [ð] between vowels — complementary distribution makes them allophones of /d/.
default.hint: Environments to consider: word-initial, between vowels, after a nasal, word-final.
default.text:
Spanish [d] and [ð] — are [d] and [ð] separate phonemes or allophones of one phoneme?

Evidence:
- donde [donda] — [d] after a nasal
- nada [naða] — [ð] between vowels
- No minimal pair exists: each sound is tied to its own phonological environment.

knobDefs.synonyms: phonology dataset, minimal pair, complementary distribution, phoneme analysis, allophony, distinctive features

knobDefs.description: Drives payout regulations per locale: 'US-CA', 'EU-DE', 'UK', etc. Declarative.

knobDefs.description: ISO 4217 currency code (USD, EUR, GBP, …) for payouts.

knobDefs.description: Smallest amount a vendor can request to cash out

knobDefs.label: Retention (years)
knobDefs.description: Years to keep payout records for compliance.

knobDefs.label: Rounding mode
knobDefs.description: Sub-cent rounding behavior for payout amounts.

knobDefs.label: Tax strategy
knobDefs.description: inclusive = tax baked into payout amount; exclusive = tax withheld separately; none = no tax.

knobDefs.description: Heading shown above the vendor payout ledger

knobDefs.description: Ramp's high (top) end x, as a fraction of width.

knobDefs.label: Ramp Bottom X Fraction
knobDefs.description: Ramp's low (bottom) end x, as a fraction of width.

knobDefs.description: Ramp's high (top) end y, as a fraction of height.

knobDefs.label: Ramp Bottom Y Fraction
knobDefs.description: Ramp's low (bottom) end y, as a fraction of height.

knobDefs.label: Curve Color
knobDefs.description: Color of the retention curve and its current-value marker.

knobDefs.label: Decay Rate
knobDefs.description: Exponential forgetting rate — each STEP_TIME multiplies retention by exp(−decayRate · Δt).
knobDefs.synonyms: forgetting rate, Ebbinghaus decay, retention decay, memory decay

knobDefs.label: Grid Step
knobDefs.description: Spacing between gridlines on the canvas, in time units.

knobDefs.label: Reference Curve Color
knobDefs.description: Color of the no-repetition reference decay curve.

knobDefs.label: Repetition Boost
knobDefs.description: Fraction of the forgotten gap (1 − retention) recovered by one repetition; the massed preset halves it to model cramming's weaker encoding.
knobDefs.synonyms: repetition effect, rehearsal boost, spacing effect, relearning savings

knobDefs.label: Schedule Preset
knobDefs.description: Practice schedule being demonstrated: massed practice (cramming) recovers only half the boost per repetition, spaced practice recovers the full boost — the spacing effect.
knobDefs.synonyms: spaced repetition, distributed practice, massed practice, cramming, spacing effect

knobDefs.label: Time Horizon
knobDefs.description: Total time units shown on the x-axis; each STEP_TIME advances one twentieth of it.

knobDefs.label: Title
knobDefs.description: Title shown above the canvas.

knobDefs.label: Curve Color
knobDefs.description: Color of the cumulative-response curve.

knobDefs.label: Grid Step
knobDefs.description: Spacing between gridlines on the canvas.

knobDefs.label: Interval Length
knobDefs.description: Time units required per reinforcer on interval schedules; VI alternates between intervalLength ± half.
knobDefs.synonyms: interval requirement, fixed interval length, inter-reinforcement interval

knobDefs.label: Ratio N
knobDefs.description: Responses required per reinforcer on ratio schedules; VR alternates between ratioN ± half.
knobDefs.synonyms: ratio requirement, fixed ratio size, response requirement

knobDefs.label: Reinforcer Color
knobDefs.description: Color of the reinforcement markers on the cumulative record.

knobDefs.label: Response Cap
knobDefs.description: Y-axis maximum of the cumulative record, in cumulative responses.

knobDefs.label: Response Rate
knobDefs.description: Responses emitted per EMIT_RESPONSE click — one lever-press batch.
knobDefs.synonyms: response burst, lever press rate, response batch

knobDefs.label: Schedule Type
knobDefs.description: Reinforcement schedule: fixed ratio (every ratioN responses), variable ratio (targets alternating around ratioN), fixed interval (every intervalLength time units), variable interval (targets alternating around intervalLength).
knobDefs.synonyms: fixed ratio, variable ratio, fixed interval, variable interval, reinforcement schedule, Skinner box, operant schedule

knobDefs.label: Time Cap
knobDefs.description: X-axis maximum of the cumulative record, in time units.

knobDefs.label: Title
knobDefs.description: Title shown above the canvas.

knobDefs.label: Base Rate
knobDefs.description: Probability that a simulated trial actually contains a signal — governs the empirical hit/false-alarm mix in RUN_TRIALS.
knobDefs.synonyms: base rate, signal prevalence, prior probability, signal probability

knobDefs.label: Criterion
knobDefs.description: Initial decision threshold on the evidence axis; evidence above it triggers a 'signal present' response. Hit rate is Φ(d′ − c), false-alarm rate Φ(−c).
knobDefs.synonyms: decision criterion, response bias, threshold, beta, cutoff

knobDefs.label: Criterion Color
knobDefs.description: Color of the criterion line and marker.

knobDefs.label: d′ (Sensitivity)
knobDefs.description: Separation between the noise and signal+noise distributions, in standard deviations — the learner's sensitivity to the signal.
knobDefs.synonyms: d prime, sensitivity, discriminability, signal strength, detectability

knobDefs.label: Noise Curve Color
knobDefs.description: Color of the noise distribution curve.

knobDefs.label: Signal Curve Color
knobDefs.description: Color of the signal+noise distribution curve.

knobDefs.label: Title
knobDefs.description: Title shown above the canvas.

knobDefs.label: Trials Per Run
knobDefs.description: Simulated detection trials per RUN_TRIALS click.

knobDefs.label: Congruent Ratio
knobDefs.description: Target proportion of congruent trials; NEXT_TRIAL steers into the incongruent pool whenever the running congruent fraction exceeds this.
knobDefs.synonyms: congruence proportion, congruent trial proportion, trial mix

knobDefs.label: Height
knobDefs.description: Canvas height in pixels.

knobDefs.label: Stimuli

knobDefs.label: Which field does the first load filter on?
knobDefs.description: Name the field the INITIAL load filters on, paired with initialFilterValue. This is the detail half of a list-detail pair: a thread that must wait for a conversation to be picked sets the field to its parent key and leaves the value blank, so the first load matches nothing and the empty state shows instead of every record in the table. REFETCH_FILTER then supplies the real selection. Left blank the first load is unfiltered, which is the default.
knobDefs.synonyms: initial filter, first load filter, wait for selection, detail pane filter, requires selection, start empty

knobDefs.label: What value does the first load filter for?
knobDefs.description: The value initialFilterField must equal on the first load. Blank is meaningful: it matches only records whose field is itself blank, which for a detail pane is normally none — that is how a thread stays empty until its parent is selected.
knobDefs.synonyms: initial filter value, first load value, default selection

knobDefs.label: Which field does the first load filter on?
knobDefs.description: Name the field the INITIAL load filters on, paired with initialFilterValue. This is the detail half of a list-detail pair: a thread that must wait for a conversation to be picked sets the field to its parent key and leaves the value blank, so the first load matches nothing and the empty state shows instead of every record in the table. REFETCH_FILTER then supplies the real selection. Left blank the first load is unfiltered, which is the default.
knobDefs.synonyms: initial filter, first load filter, wait for selection, detail pane filter, requires selection, start empty

knobDefs.label: What value does the first load filter for?
knobDefs.description: The value initialFilterField must equal on the first load. Blank is meaningful: it matches only records whose field is itself blank, which for a detail pane is normally none — that is how a thread stays empty until its parent is selected.
knobDefs.synonyms: initial filter value, first load value, default selection

knobDefs.label: Print form
knobDefs.description: Trait that renders the print job UI

knobDefs.label: Body
knobDefs.description: Notification body text.

knobDefs.label: Icon
knobDefs.description: Notification icon URL.

knobDefs.label: Subscription
knobDefs.description: Browser PushSubscription: endpoint URL plus the p256dh/auth encryption keys.

knobDefs.label: Title
knobDefs.description: Notification title.

knobDefs.label: Operation form
knobDefs.description: Trait that renders the Web Push operation UI

knobDefs.label: Url
knobDefs.description: URL to open when the notification is clicked.

knobDefs.label: Delay
knobDefs.description: Delay before the job becomes eligible for dequeue, in milliseconds.

knobDefs.label: Error
knobDefs.description: Failure reason to attach to the job.

knobDefs.label: Job Id
knobDefs.description: Job id from enqueue.

knobDefs.label: Operation
knobDefs.description: Which Message Queue action to run: enqueue, dequeue, status, complete, fail, cancel, size

knobDefs.label: Payload
knobDefs.description: Job payload — the caller declares its own shape.

knobDefs.label: Priority
knobDefs.description: Priority — higher values are dequeued before lower ones.

knobDefs.label: Queue
knobDefs.description: Queue name.

knobDefs.label: Result
knobDefs.description: Result payload to attach to the job — the caller declares its own shape (not necessarily the same shape as the job's `payload`).

knobDefs.label: Operation form
knobDefs.description: Trait that renders the Message Queue operation UI

knobDefs.label: By
knobDefs.description: Amount to add; defaults to 1 (can be negative to decrement).

knobDefs.label: Channel
knobDefs.description: Channel name.

knobDefs.label: Key
knobDefs.description: Cache key.

knobDefs.label: Lock Id
knobDefs.description: Lock id returned by the corresponding `lock` call.

knobDefs.label: Message
knobDefs.description: Message payload — the caller declares its own shape.

knobDefs.label: Operation
knobDefs.description: Which Redis Cache action to run: get, set, delete, lock, unlock, increment, expire, publish, subscribe

knobDefs.label: Ttl
knobDefs.description: Time-to-live in seconds; omit for no expiry.

knobDefs.label: Operation form
knobDefs.description: Trait that renders the Redis Cache operation UI

knobDefs.label: Value
knobDefs.description: Value to store — the caller declares its own shape.

knobDefs.label: Categories
knobDefs.description: The three-way labeling-theory classification ladder, bottom (most common, least deviant) to top (least common, most deviant): conforming acts, primary deviance (norm violation with only informal sanction, no label), and secondary deviance (a formal label applied and internalized).
knobDefs.synonyms: deviance, labeling theory, Lemert, primary deviance, secondary deviance, formal sanction, informal sanction, social control, conforming

default.explanation: Lemert's primary deviance: a norm was violated and mildly sanctioned, but no deviant label was applied or internalized — the act passes without reshaping anyone's identity or status.

options.label: Conforming — no norm was really broken.
Primary deviance — norm violation, minor informal sanction, no label.
Secondary deviance — a formal label was internalized.

default.text: A driver is ticketed for speeding, pays the fine, and thinks no more of it; neither does anyone else.

default.explanation: Secondary deviance (Lemert): once the formal label is applied by the justice system and internalized, the deviant identity organizes further behavior — deviance amplified by the societal reaction itself, the core claim of labeling theory.

options.label: Primary deviance — the label never stuck.
Conforming — he was only adjusting to expectations.
Secondary deviance — the formal label was applied and internalized, organizing further deviance.

default.text: A teenager caught shoplifting is arrested, formally charged, and comes to be treated — and to see himself — as a 'delinquent'; he re-offends.

default.explanation: Primary deviance: a minor norm violation that draws no sanction and no label. Most people commit such acts occasionally without any consequence for their identity — deviance is common; being labeled deviant is rare.

options.label: Primary deviance — a minor violation with no sanction and no label.
Secondary deviance — the label reshapes her identity.
Conforming — taking office supplies is fully normative.

default.text: An office worker takes a pen home from the supply closet; everyone does it, nobody comments, and it is never punished.

default.explanation: Conforming: the act follows the governing norms (policy and professional ethics) rather than violating them. That the supervisor disliked it does not make it deviant — deviance is defined against the group's norms, not a superior's preference.

options.label: Primary deviance — refusing a superior is always a violation.
Conforming — the act follows the governing norms and is rewarded.
Secondary deviance — the commendation is a label.

default.text: A nurse refuses an unsafe order from a supervisor because hospital policy and professional ethics forbid it, and is formally commended.

knobDefs.synonyms: deviance, labeling theory, Lemert, primary deviance, secondary deviance, formal sanction, informal sanction, social control

knobDefs.label: What should this task manager be called?
knobDefs.description: Shown in the top-left of the app and the browser tab.
knobDefs.synonyms: app title, product name, brand name, application name, site name

knobDefs.label: Which sections appear in the task manager sidebar?
knobDefs.synonyms: board, list, calendar, dashboard, activity, sections, navigation
knobDefs.description: Top-level navigation links shown on the left rail.

knobDefs.label: Idle content
knobDefs.description: The normal content view (e.g. the data ledger/browse trait) shown when no search is active.

knobDefs.label: Result columns
knobDefs.description: Columns shown in the search-results grid; maps entity fields to display cells.

knobDefs.label: Show the log's own search box?
knobDefs.description: Embeds a search box above the activity feed. Set true only when the page has no other search affordance (e.g. no page-level std-search), so the surface shows one search box instead of two. False is the default — no consumer of this atom has ever had a search box.
knobDefs.synonyms: inline search, log search, built-in search, show search

knobDefs.label: How many entries per page should a pager show?
knobDefs.description: Page size a consumer-composed std-pagination control should use to compute total pages (e.g. from totalCount). This atom's own timeline pattern has no built-in pager UI, so this knob is informational for the composed control, not consumed by the timeline itself.
knobDefs.synonyms: visible rows, items per page, display limit

knobDefs.label: Which filters should appear above the feed?
knobDefs.description: Dropdown filter facets by field, rendered as an embedded filter bar above the timeline; each selection fires REFETCH_FILTER on this trait, ANDed with the current kind tab. Empty (the default) = no filter bar — the right setting whenever the page already composes std-filter beside this atom and routes XFilter.FILTER -> REFETCH_FILTER, or relies solely on the built-in kind-filter chips (driven by kindOptions, which this knob does not duplicate or replace). Use this knob only for an extra facet beyond kind (e.g. actor, priority).
knobDefs.synonyms: filter bar, faceted filters, field filters, dropdowns

knobDefs.label: Backfill fields
knobDefs.description: Inputs shown in the form for manually logging missed events

knobDefs.label: Event kinds
knobDefs.description: Maps each event kind to its label, icon, and status color

knobDefs.label: How many entries per page when paging?
knobDefs.description: Records fetched from the server per REFETCH_PAGE request. The initial load and every search/kind/filter refetch stay unpaginated (load everything that matches) so the default unlimited activity feed is unchanged; only an explicit REFETCH_PAGE from a composed std-pagination control applies this limit.
knobDefs.synonyms: fetch limit, records per page, page limit

knobDefs.label: Search box placeholder text
knobDefs.description: Hint text inside the log's search box.
knobDefs.synonyms: search hint, placeholder, search box text

knobDefs.label: Timeline look
knobDefs.description: Layer 2 visual treatment for the timeline.

knobDefs.label: Section title
knobDefs.description: Heading shown above the activity timeline

knobDefs.label: Content trait
knobDefs.description: Trait rendered inside the app layout content area

knobDefs.label: Idle content
knobDefs.description: The normal content view (e.g. the data ledger/browse trait) shown when no search is active.

knobDefs.label: Columns
knobDefs.description: Board columns; each row's stage maps to a column key

knobDefs.label: New-card fields
knobDefs.description: Fields shown in the add-card form

knobDefs.label: Board title
knobDefs.description: Heading shown above the column board

knobDefs.label: Which fields appear in the form?
knobDefs.description: Entity fields rendered as inputs inside the modal form.
knobDefs.synonyms: form fields, inputs, editable fields, field list

knobDefs.label: Trigger events
knobDefs.description: Event names that should fire a notification. Set this to the upstream event name (e.g. OrderPlaced, CheckoutCompleted) so this atom listens for events from the orbital that emits them. The orbital owning this trait reacts whenever the named event fires anywhere in the schema.
knobDefs.synonyms: subscribe to event, listen for event, react to event, watch for, wire upstream event, observe event from another orbital, cross-orbital subscription, on-event trigger

knobDefs.label: What should this app be called?
knobDefs.description: Name shown in the top-left of the chrome header.
knobDefs.synonyms: app title, product name, brand name, application name, site name

knobDefs.label: Content trait
knobDefs.description: Trait rendered inside the app layout content area

knobDefs.label: Which sections appear in the sidebar?
knobDefs.description: Top-level navigation links shown on the left rail.
knobDefs.synonyms: nav links, menu items, sidebar sections, navigation entries, pages

knobDefs.label: Idle content
knobDefs.description: The normal content view (e.g. the data ledger/browse trait) shown when no search is active.

knobDefs.label: Calendar layout
knobDefs.description: How tasks are laid out: month grid, day-grouped agenda list, or 7-column week timeline.
knobDefs.synonyms: month view, agenda view, week view, schedule layout

knobDefs.label: On Event Click
knobDefs.description: Event emitted when a calendar chip is clicked: UI:{onEventClick} with { event } carrying the clicked row. Empty means chips are not clickable.
knobDefs.synonyms: open event, event click, select event, chip click

knobDefs.label: Start field
knobDefs.description: Row column holding the timestamp the calendar grid places each chip by. Rebound hosts point this at their own column (e.g. startTime, startsAt, dueAt); the chip's LABEL comes from titleBinding, not from here.
knobDefs.synonyms: start column, date column, when field, timestamp field

knobDefs.label: Title
knobDefs.description: Header text shown above the calendar body.

knobDefs.label: Content trait
knobDefs.description: Trait rendered inside the app layout content area

knobDefs.label: Metrics
knobDefs.description: One stat card per entry; declares aggregation, format, and styling
knobDefs.synonyms: list of KPI cards / stat tiles / metric cards. each entry has label / value / format / icon / variant / aggregation. user phrases: 'replace metrics with X, Y, Z' -> rewrite array; 'add Revenue tile' -> append entry; 'change KPIs to X' -> rewrite array

knobDefs.label: Section title
knobDefs.description: Heading shown above the stat-card grid

knobDefs.label: Channel
knobDefs.description: Delivery channel. `in-app` (default) emits the in-app `notify` toast. `email`/`sms`/`webhook` dispatch through call-service at event time (email.send / twilio.sendSMS / webhook.send) and persist a NotificationRecord audit row with an honest `dispatched` flag: true only once the service call succeeds, false plus the failure detail in `error` otherwise. `push` looks up the recipient's PushSubscription row (captured by std-notification-center's subscribe flow) and dispatches web-push via push.send — a recipient with no subscription records the audit row undispatched (`no-push-subscription`). `webhook` requires `webhookUrl` to actually dispatch; a blank `webhookUrl` still records the audit row undispatched rather than failing. A per-user NotificationPreference row's `channel` overrides this value for that recipient.

knobDefs.label: Who can approve requests?

knobDefs.synonyms: approver, reviewer, authorized roles, sign-off roles, who approves

knobDefs.label: Block approving your own requests?
knobDefs.description: When on, a reviewer cannot APPROVE a request they submitted themselves (requestedBy = the viewer's id) — enforced by the APPROVE transition guard, from the button or from the bus. Requires hosts to stamp requestedBy at request creation. DENY stays allowed on your own request (denying your own request withdraws it). Off by default.
knobDefs.synonyms: self approval, self-approval, four eyes, four-eyes, separation of duties, cannot approve own, no self sign-off, dual control

Toolbar (search when bodySearch, filter bar when filters is non-empty) above the canonical data-grid call. Until 2026-08-27 this was the only one of the six looks with no search affordance at all. Inlined directly (not via a composed sibling trait) 2026-09-08 — a separately-listening DataGrid1 sibling fired unconditionally on every BrowseItemLoaded regardless of browseLook, racing the correct body for slot main (a listens guard can't gate this: both the Rust interpreter and the TS codegen path restrict a listens guard's context to @payload only, so a browseLook config check there always evaluates undefined).

knobDefs.label: Facing
knobDefs.description: The orientation token for the whole art bible — which authored projection of part geometry renders: front orthographic, right-facing side profile, front-right 3/4 quarter, or rear-view back. Unlike style (same geometry, different treatment), each facing is re-authored geometry; part molecules branch their geometry on it exactly as they branch recipes on style, and catalog states nest per facing. Left-facing is a runtime mirror of side, never authored.

knobDefs.label: Lighting Model
knobDefs.description: How form renders: light always from lightDir; specular = white ellipse of specularSize cell units at specularAlpha near the lit side; form shading = white→transparent highlight at highlightAlpha from the light, black→transparent core shadow at coreShadowAlpha on the far side.

knobDefs.label: Material Recipes
knobDefs.description: How each named material renders, as palette-step names (resolved against the chosen palette): gradient kind + stop sequence, specular treatment (band | sparkle | dot | none), whether it glows (shadow blur) or pulses (opacity animation), and whether it takes a silhouette contour.

knobDefs.label: Stroke Policy
knobDefs.description: Line-weight hierarchy in painter px: outer silhouette contours thickest, inner detail strokes thinner, terrain cell edges thinnest. Contour color is ALWAYS the palette's ambientShadow at contourAlpha — never pure black.

knobDefs.label: Style Direction
knobDefs.description: The theme direction token for the whole art bible — the recipe branch every material/part molecule renders the same geometry+palette through: glossy house style (gradients + specular + contour), pure minimal flat (flat fills + one shine dot), heavy-outline cartoon (6px contour + big shine), neon (glow strokes, no fill), paper cutout (flat fills backed by hard offset shadow copies), or noir (near-black fills + a rim-light stroke fading from the lit corner). One flip restyles every material-composed asset; generated authoring preambles (§13) interpolate it.
